findings.element: Actions cell of Done rows in the Line Analysis and Trip Failures accordions
findings.finding: Five of the seventeen finished evaluations offer no way to open a result — all three Done Line Analysis rows and two of the four Done Trip Failures rows carry Delete as their only action.
findings.user_impact: A user who finds one of these evaluations, sees a green Done chip and tries to open its report has no route to it, and the single action the row does offer destroys the evaluation.
findings.suggested_fix: Render the preview action on every Done row — the app already routes line_analysis and trip_failures reports to working report views — or replace the Done chip on rows with no viewable result with a state that says why.

evidence.action: Expanded the Line Analysis and Trip Failures accordions and read the Actions cell of every row showing a Done status chip.
evidence.observed: All 3 Done Line Analysis rows and 2 of the 4 Done Trip Failures rows render only the delete icon — no preview, no download — while the other 2 Done Trip Failures rows render preview + delete; the state map records the same sets (done:line_analysis and done:trip_failures resolve to delete only).

findings.element: Download icon on Done rows in the Raw Data Export accordion
findings.finding: Download announces "Download started …" in a snackbar but never produces a file, so the UI reports success for an action that did not happen.
findings.user_impact: For a Raw Data Export the file is the result, so the user is told the job is done, waits, finds nothing in their downloads and re-clicks with no error or progress to explain the failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Either produce the file on click, or replace the success snackbar with a state that says the export is not available and what the user should do instead.

evidence.action: Clicked the download icon on a Done Raw Data Export row.
evidence.observed: A snackbar reads "Download started …" and nothing further happens — no file is produced and the row is unchanged; the click handler only raises the notification.

findings.element: Top-bar nav links (Startseite, Q.Reports, Fotoalbum, Q-Messungen) and the login utility links (Impressum, Dokumente, Kontaktdaten, Support) plus "Forgot your password?"
findings.finding: Nine controls that read as navigation are inert — they do not navigate, show no message and give no disabled treatment strong enough to read as one.
findings.user_impact: Users click the most prominent navigation on the screen, get no response at all, and cannot tell whether the app is broken, the click missed, or the destination is simply absent — the exact dead-click pattern KF-4 records as the densest in production.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the out-of-scope nav items a genuine disabled treatment with a tooltip naming why they are unavailable, and drop the open-in-new-tab icon from any link that has no target.

evidence.action: Clicked each of the four top-bar nav links, the four login utility links, and "Forgot your password?".
evidence.observed: All nine did nothing — no navigation, no message, no state change; the nav links sit at 75% opacity and the four login utility links each display an open-in-new-tab icon that promises a destination they do not have.

findings.element: Evaluation name cell in the table, against the eye icon in the Actions column
findings.finding: The evaluation name — the thing the user is looking for and the obvious click target — is inert text, and the only entry point to a report is a small eye icon at the far right end of the row.
findings.user_impact: Having located the evaluation they want, the user clicks its name, gets nothing, and must discover that the route to the report is an unlabelled icon at the opposite end of the row; combined with UX-1 they must inspect the rightmost cell of each of 28 rows to learn which evaluations open at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the evaluation name a link to the report on every row that carries a preview action, pointing at the same destination as the eye icon.

evidence.action: Clicked the evaluation name text in a Done Punctuality row, then clicked the eye icon in the Actions column of that same row.
evidence.observed: The name is plain text and produced no response; only the eye icon opened the report.

gaps: New evaluation: the state map lists "Run" in not_exercised, so the second half of the primary task — actually creating an evaluation and seeing it land in the list — has no recorded commit behaviour. Only the page opening with Run disabled is confirmed.

Report views: the state map lists "Report views beyond the first screen" in not_exercised, so for the rows that do open, whether the user reaches a usable result is unverified — the end state of the primary task is unconfirmed.

The state map's row-action map is keyed by status:group, which collapses rows that differ inside one group: it records done:trip_failures as "delete" and so hides that 2 of the 4 Done Trip Failures rows do carry a preview action. A lens reading only that map would miss the inconsistency in UX-1.

Live interaction was unavailable to me this round (browser scope closed, and the page is client-rendered so the fetched HTML carries no row data). UX-1's row-by-row counts were therefore confirmed against the prototype's own row data rather than by clicking each row; every finding's named interaction is still reproducible in the running app.

Status filter: the data carries four statuses (done, in_progress, running, failed) but only three labels, since in_progress and running both display "In Progress". The filter matches on the label rather than the raw value, so no row is silently dropped — checked and clear, but recorded here because the state map's three-option dropdown does not reveal the fourth status.
